CONTEXT
- Task: a C++ program /workspace/dataset/test11.cpp (uses the mapbox earcut.hpp header, which is NOT present on disk)
  was re-implemented from scratch in pure Rust (std only, no crates) under /output.
- Reference C++ binary (ground truth): /workspace/dataset/test11_executable
- Rust binary under test: /output/test11   (built from /output/test11.rs with: cd /output && rustc -O test11.rs -o test11)
- Rust sources: /output/test11.rs, /output/cli.rs, /output/gear.rs, /output/earcut/{mod,node,geom,zorder,triangulate}.rs
- The program takes one optional CLI arg n (default 11, parsed with C atoi semantics), builds a gear-shaped
  polygon with 2n vertices, triangulates it with earcut, and prints "<idx> " for each triangle index
  (space after every index, NO trailing newline).
- Requirement: the Rust stdout must be BYTE-FOR-BYTE identical to the C++ stdout for the same argv.

HARD RULES
- DO NOT modify, delete, rebuild or write anything under /output. It is READ-ONLY for you.
  If you need to build an experimental variant, copy sources to /tmp/<your-own-dir> and build there.
- Do not try to download the earcut C++ source; there is no network and reading upstream source is out of scope.
  Treat the C++ binary purely as a black box oracle.
- Always guard reference-binary runs with a timeout, e.g. `timeout 60 /workspace/dataset/test11_executable 5000`.
  Very large n (e.g. > ~500000) can run for minutes; do not hang the workflow.
- Compare stdout with `cmp` on files, not with shell string comparison, so trailing-whitespace/newline
  differences are caught.
- There is a ready-made harness: /workspace/difftest.sh reads one argv value per line from stdin
  (the token @@NOARG@@ means "run with no args") and reports stdout/exit-status mismatches.
  Example: `seq 400 600 | /workspace/difftest.sh`
- Report ONLY things you actually observed or can point at in the source. No speculation presented as fact.


YOUR TASK (sweep:cli-fuzz):
Fuzz the command line argument handling. Compare /output/test11 against the reference for AT LEAST these
argv[1] values, byte-for-byte on stdout AND exit status AND stderr:
no argument at all; "" (empty string); "0"; "-0"; "+0"; "-1"; "-7"; "007"; "  7"; "\t7"; "\n7"; "7  ";
"7abc"; "abc"; "abc7"; "3.9"; "-3.9"; "0x10"; "010"; "1e3"; "+ 7"; "- 7"; "--7"; "++7";
"2147483647"; "2147483648"; "-2147483648"; "-2147483649"; "4294967296"; "4294967299"; "4294967337";
"9223372036854775807"; "9223372036854775808"; "-9223372036854775808"; "-9223372036854775809";
"99999999999999999999"; a string of 400 '9' digits; "0000000000000000000000005";
"9223372036854775807abc"; "-4294967293"; "  +11  ".
ALSO test extra arguments being present: e.g. `prog 5 99` and `prog 5 abc` (only argv[1] should matter).
Use a shell loop writing outputs to files and cmp'ing them. Beware: values that decode to a huge positive n
will hang — anything that decodes above ~200000 should be run with `timeout 20` and, if BOTH binaries time out,
recorded as "both hang (consistent)" rather than a mismatch. Report every discrepancy with the exact argv.

Return structured findings. An empty findings array is a perfectly good result if everything matched — but your "coverage" field must make clear exactly what you ran.

#!/bin/bash
# Differential test harness: compares /output/test11 against the reference C++
# binary byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr and exit status) for a list of argv[1]
# values supplied on stdin (one raw value per line; the literal token
# @@NOARG@@ means "invoke with no arguments").
REF=/workspace/dataset/test11_executable
RUST=/output/test11
fail=0
count=0
while IFS= read -r arg; do
  count=$((count+1))
  if [ "$arg" == "@@NOARG@@" ]; then
    "$REF"  >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  else
    "$REF"  "$arg" >/tmp/ref.out 2>/tmp/ref.err; rs=$?
    "$RUST" "$arg" >/tmp/rus.out 2>/tmp/rus.err; ns=$?
  fi
  if ! cmp -s /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out; then
    echo "STDOUT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]"
    echo "  ref bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/ref.out)  rust bytes: $(wc -c </tmp/rus.out)"
    cmp /tmp/ref.out /tmp/rus.out | head -2
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
  if [ "$rs" != "$ns" ]; then
    echo "EXIT MISMATCH for arg=[$arg]: ref=$rs rust=$ns"
    fail=$((fail+1))
  fi
done
echo "checked=$count failures=$fail"
[ "$fail" -eq 0 ]

#!/bin/bash
source /tmp/fuzz/cases.sh
REF=/workspace/dataset/test11_executable
RUST=/output/test11
OUT=/tmp/fuzz/out
mkdir -p "$OUT"
SKIP="${SKIP:-}"
TMO="${TMO:-20}"
fails=0
for i in "${!NAMES[@]}"; do
  nm="${NAMES[$i]}"
  case " $SKIP " in *" $nm "*) echo "SKIP  $nm"; continue;; esac
  case "${MODES[$i]}" in
    NOARG) timeout "$TMO" "$REF"  >"$OUT/$nm.ref.out" 2>"$OUT/$nm.ref.err"; rs=$?
           timeout "$TMO" "$RUST" >"$OUT/$nm.rus.out" 2>"$OUT/$nm.rus.err"; ns=$? ;;
    ARG)   timeout "$TMO" "$REF"  "${VALS[$i]}" >"$OUT/$nm.ref.out" 2>"$OUT/$nm.ref.err"; rs=$?
           timeout "$TMO" "$RUST" "${VALS[$i]}" >"$OUT/$nm.rus.out" 2>"$OUT/$nm.rus.err"; ns=$? ;;
    ARG2)  timeout "$TMO" "$REF"  "${VALS[$i]}" "${VALS2[$i]}" >"$OUT/$nm.ref.out" 2>"$OUT/$nm.ref.err"; rs=$?
           timeout "$TMO" "$RUST" "${VALS[$i]}" "${VALS2[$i]}" >"$OUT/$nm.rus.out" 2>"$OUT/$nm.rus.err"; ns=$? ;;
  esac
  bad=""
  cmp -s "$OUT/$nm.ref.out" "$OUT/$nm.rus.out" || bad="$bad STDOUT"
  cmp -s "$OUT/$nm.ref.err" "$OUT/$nm.rus.err" || bad="$bad STDERR"
  [ "$rs" == "$ns" ] || bad="$bad EXIT(ref=$rs rust=$ns)"
  rb=$(wc -c <"$OUT/$nm.ref.out"); ub=$(wc -c <"$OUT/$nm.rus.out")
  reb=$(wc -c <"$OUT/$nm.ref.err"); ueb=$(wc -c <"$OUT/$nm.rus.err")
  if [ -n "$bad" ]; then
    echo "FAIL  $nm ->$bad  (ref_out=$rb rust_out=$ub ref_err=$reb rust_err=$ueb)"

    fails=$((fails+1))
  else
    echo "ok    $nm  exit=$rs out=${rb}B err=${reb}B"
  fi
done
echo "=== failures=$fails ==="
EOS

findings.title: OOM-path stderr text differs (C++ bad_alloc terminate vs Rust handle_alloc_error) — only observable under an imposed RLIMIT_AS; stdout and exit status still match
findings.detail:
argv[1]="2147483647" and argv[1]="-2147483649" both decode (verified against a C atoi oracle) to n=2147483647, requiring ~68.7 GB for the 2n-vertex ring. Run naturally (with a 90 GB address-space guard purely to protect the host) BOTH binaries behave identically: exit 124 after the 20 s timeout, 0 bytes on stdout, 0 bytes on stderr -> "both hang (consistent)", no discrepancy. The divergence only appears if allocation is forced to fail fast: under an identical `ulimit -v 2000000` (2 GB) both abort with exit status 134 and byte-identical (empty) stdout, but stderr differs — reference prints "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::bad_alloc'
  what():  std::bad_alloc
" while the Rust binary prints "memory allocation of 2147483648 bytes failed
". This is inherent to the two runtimes' allocation-failure handlers, is not reachable without an externally imposed memory limit, and does not affect the stated requirement (stdout byte-for-byte). Reported only because the task asked for stderr to be compared byte-for-byte. Note also a latent asymmetry that did not manifest: the C++ `polygon.push_back(gear)` copies the ring (peak ~137 GB) whereas Rust's `polygon.push(gear)` moves it (peak ~103 GB), so on a machine with 103-137 GB free the C++ side could OOM where Rust succeeds.
findings.repro: for a in 2147483647 -2147483649; do ( ulimit -v 2000000; timeout 30 /workspace/dataset/test11_executable "$a" >/tmp/h.ro 2>/tmp/h.re ); echo "ref=$?"; ( ulimit -v 2000000; timeout 30 /output/test11 "$a" >/tmp/h.uo 2>/tmp/h.ue ); echo "rust=$?"; cmp /tmp/h.ro /tmp/h.uo; cmp /tmp/h.re /tmp/h.ue; done   # stdout identical (0B), exit 134 both, stderr differs.  Unconstrained control: ( ulimit -v 90000000; timeout -k 2 20 /workspace/dataset/test11_executable 2147483647 ) -> exit 124, 0B/0B; same for /output/test11 -> exit 124, 0B/0B (both hang, consistent)

input.coverage:
SCOPE: CLI/argv fuzzing only. Compared /output/test11 (md5 87824a3787bb3561dc1e19598dd7082a, built 16:24:22 — verified unchanged before and after every sweep) against /workspace/dataset/test11_executable, always on stdout AND stderr AND exit status, using `cmp` on files (never shell string comparison).

IMPORTANT — SOURCES CHANGED MID-SESSION: when I started, /output/test11.rs used `std::env::args()` and /output/cli.rs had no OsString handling. At 16:24 another actor rewrote them to `std::env::args_os()` + `to_string_lossy()` (see the doc comment now at /output/cli.rs:59-66) and rebuilt the binary. I re-ran EVERY sweep from scratch against the post-16:24 binary; all results below are for that binary. I verified with a standalone probe that `std::env::args().nth(1)` on rustc 1.75.0 panics (exit 101) on non-UTF-8 argv, so the pre-16:24 version would have diverged on e.g. argv[1]=$'\\xff7'; the current args_os+lossy version does not.

HARNESSES (all in /tmp, nothing written under /output):
- /tmp/fuzz/cases.sh + /tmp/fuzz/run.sh — the 41 required argv values as a bash array (so tabs/newlines/trailing spaces survive intact), plus the two extra-arg cases.
- /tmp/fuzz/extra.sh, /tmp/utf8edge.sh, /tmp/long.sh — extended edge cases.
- /tmp/rfuzz.sh + /tmp/gen.c, /tmp/gen2.c — randomized fuzzers (hex-encoded argv so arbitrary bytes round-trip).
- /tmp/atoichk2 (C: prints atoi/strtol/errno) used as an independent oracle for the decoded n of every value.
- /tmp/dump.c to confirm raw bytes actually reach argv.
- /tmp/argc0.c to execve with an empty argv (argc==0).

REQUIRED LIST — 41/41 PASS byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr, exit=0), with the decoded n confirmed via the C atoi oracle:
no-arg(n=11,154B), ""(0), "0"(0), "-0"(0), "+0"(0), "-1", "-7", "007"(7,83B), "  7"(7), "\t7"(7), "\n7"(7), "7  "(7), "7abc"(7), "abc"(0), "abc7"(0), "3.9"(3,24B), "-3.9"(-3), "0x10"(0), "010"(10,136B), "1e3"(1), "+ 7"(0), "- 7"(0), "--7"(0), "++7"(0), "2147483648"(-2147483648), "-2147483648", "4294967296"(0), "4294967299"(3), "4294967337"(41,690B), "9223372036854775807"(-1), "9223372036854775808"(-1), "-9223372036854775808"(0), "-9223372036854775809"(0), "99999999999999999999"(-1), 400x'9'(-1), "0000000000000000000000005"(5,48B), "9223372036854775807abc"(-1), "-4294967293"(3), "  +11  "(11,154B). Extra args: `prog 5 99` and `prog 5 abc` both give the n=5 output (48B), so only argv[1] matters.
The two remaining required values, "2147483647" and "-2147483649" (both -> n=2147483647), are the subject of the single finding: both hang consistently (exit 124, 0B stdout, 0B stderr) at timeout 20.

I also spot-verified the actual bytes: outputs end with a trailing space and NO trailing newline (od -c on the tails), n=11 gives the expected 154-byte line, n=3 gives "4 5 0 0 1 2 2 3 4 4 0 2 " matching the fixture's Example 1.

EXTRA CLI CASES — 27/27 PASS: $'\\v7', $'\\f7', $'\\r7', $' \\t\\n\\v\\f\\r 7', "+", "-", "     ", "\t", ".5", " -5", "5\n", "\n", "9223372036854775806", Arabic-Indic "٧", "é7", NBSP+"7", raw $'\\xff', $'\\xff7', $'7\\xff', $'\\x807', $'\\xe97', ("" "5"), ("5" ""), ("5" "99" "abc" "-1" "7"), ("--" "5"), "-h", "--help".

NON-UTF-8 / LOSSY-DECODE EDGE CASES — 20/20 PASS: truncated lead bytes $'\\xe07' $'\\xf07' $'\\xc27', surrogate $'\\xed\\xa0\\x807', overlong $'\\xc0\\x807', $'\\xf4\\x907', $'7\\xe0', $'  \\xff7', $'\\xff  7', $'-\\xff7', $'5\\xc3', $'\\xc3\\x285', $'\\xfe\\xff7', $'7\\x009', UTF-8 BOM+"7", U+FFFD+"7", $'9\\xff9', $'\\x80\\x81\\x82', "ééç", 50x$'\\xff'+"7". Plus Unicode-whitespace prefixes (U+3000, U+2000, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+00A0, U+2009) — all correctly treated as non-whitespace by both (n=0), confirming the C-locale isspace set in /output/cli.rs:54.

DEGENERATE ARGC / ARGV[0]: execve with argv={NULL} (argc==0) -> both print the n=11 default, 154B, identical stdout+stderr+exit. `exec -a "weird name" ... 5` -> identical.

VERY LONG ARGV — 9/9 PASS: 100000 '9's, "7"+100000 'x', 100000 '0's+"7", 100000 spaces+"7", 100000 'x', ("5" + 100000 '9's), ("5" "2147483647"), ("5" "-2147483649"), ("11" a b c d e f g).

RANDOMIZED FUZZ — 2200/2200 PASS: 1200 random strings over a digit/sign/whitespace/junk charset (seed 12345) and 1000 random strings over the full 0x01-0xFF byte range with weighted digits/signs/whitespace (seed 777); both generators filter out candidates decoding to |n|>3000 to bound runtime, and every case was compared on stdout+stderr+exit.

CROSS-CHECK with the provided harness: `seq 0 60 | /workspace/difftest.sh` -> checked=61 failures=0, and a 20-value subset of the required list piped through it -> checked=20 failures=0, agreeing with my own harness.
